newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee meeting to discuss market - official.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee meeting to discuss market - official.

text.p: Brazilian government officials expect to discuss the world coffee market with a visiting African delegation at a meeting tomorrow but there will be no decisions regarding reducing exports, said Brazil's top coffee official.

"The only decision that can be taken tomorrow is whether there should be an emergency meeting (of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries) to discuss the world market," said Mauricio Assis, head of the Industry and Commerce's primary commodities department.
Assis and officials of the Foreign Affairs Ministry are to meet with a six-member delegation led by Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze at 1200 local/1400 GMT in Brasilia.
No members of the Brazilian private coffee sector will be present, Assis said.
The meeting follows a visit by the delegation to Colombia where representatives agreed on a need to cut exports by ACPC members in the first half of 1997 by around 2.5 million 60-kg bags.
Assis declined to comment on the proposal.
"We have to talk about it. This is something we would need to be very certain about," Assis said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
